name: Saffron
description: A single-file H5 recipe, meal-plan and shopping app. Every recipe is written for a base number of servings, and changing the servings rescales every quantity, rounding to something you can actually measure: whole grams, quarter spoons, half onions. The shopping list is where that arithmetic shows — add two recipes that both want onions and one line carries the total, with both recipes named against it. Cupboard staples can be left off entirely. 8 screens, 8 recipes, 39 ingredients across 6 aisles, a seven-day planner and a step-by-step cook mode. Every illustration is generated from the recipe's own palette; there is not one image file in the environment.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — scaled quantities, the shopping list and the cooking step all serialise, so a text-only agent can scale a recipe and read the result back.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view with quantities in thousandths of the display unit. For the verifier only.

world.quantities: integers in thousandths of the display unit; 1.5 tbsp is 1500 and two lots of it are exactly 3000
world.scaling: quantity x servings / base, snapped to the unit's step — 1 g, 0.25 tsp, 0.5 of an onion or a clove — and never below one step
world.aggregation: the shopping list holds one line per ingredient; adding a second recipe that wants it adds to the line and records which recipes asked for it
world.staples: salt, black pepper and olive oil are cupboard staples and are left off the list unless the setting says otherwise
